title: Procurement and Supply Chain Manager
jobDescription: Every robot we ship depends on parts arriving on time, from the right vendors, at the right price, and that takes a procurement function that is organised, sharp, and well managed. As a Procurement and Supply Chain Manager, you will own purchasing, vendor management, and the stores and inventory function. You will source and qualify vendors, negotiate terms, manage the day-to-day procurement workflow, and lead a small team responsible for purchasing, stores, and inventory. If you have spent real time chasing parts, sweating delivery dates, and negotiating with vendors, and you enjoy bringing structure to a function that needs it, this role is built for you. Day-to-Day Activities Own end-to-end procurement: from purchase requisition through PO, delivery, and invoice Identify, qualify, and onboard new vendors for mechanical, electronic, electrical, and consumable supplies Negotiate pricing, payment terms, and delivery commitments with vendors Manage vendor relationships and resolve quality, delivery, and commercial issues Manage the stores function, including goods receipt, inspection, storage, and issue Maintain accurate inventory records and oversee periodic physical stock verification Plan and manage stock levels to avoid both shortages and excess Manage and mentor a small team handling purchasing, stores, and inventory operations Track and report procurement metrics: on-time delivery, vendor performance, savings, and inventory turns Coordinate closely with engineering, production, and finance on requirements and budgets Maintain procurement documentation, contracts, and audit-ready records

title: Electronics Intern
jobDescription: Every robot we send to the field depends on electronics that survive shock, vibration, heat, and dust without missing a beat. As an Electronics Intern, you will work alongside our electronics team on the boards, harnesses, and power systems that bring our UGVs to life. This is a hands-on role on the bench and on the robot, board bring-up, sensor integration, wiring, and the kind of patient debugging that finds the fault before the field does. If you have soldered your own projects, debugged circuits past midnight, and have real instincts for how hardware behaves, this internship is built for you. Key Responsibilities Assist in PCB bring-up, inspection, and bench testing of UGV electronic subsystems Build, route, and test wiring harnesses and interconnects for robot platforms Integrate and verify sensors: IMUs, encoders, current sensors, cameras, and GPS modules Support power distribution and battery management testing and validation Run structured bench tests and capture measurements with multimeters, oscilloscopes, and power supplies Debug circuit-level faults across boards, connectors, and cabling Document schematics, pinouts, test procedures, and results clearly and systematically Support the integration and field teams during robot assembly and commissioning

title: Robotics Intern
jobDescription: Our robots have to perceive, decide, and move reliably in the messiest environments, and that takes robotics engineers who can work across autonomy, perception, and controls. As a Robotics Intern, you will support the development, integration, and testing of robotic subsystems on real UGV platforms. You will spend time in simulation, on the bench, and in the field, turning algorithms into behaviour you can watch a robot perform. If you have built robots, lived inside ROS, and run your own simulations, this internship is built for you. Key Responsibilities Support the development and testing of robotic subsystems across UGV platforms Work with ROS / ROS2 to build, run, and debug robot software components Assist in sensor integration and calibration: Li DAR, cameras, IMU, and GPS Set up and run simulation and field tests for navigation, perception, and control algorithms Collect, organise, and analyse test data to evaluate robot behaviour Help reproduce, diagnose, and document failures observed in testing Document workflows, configurations, and results systematically Collaborate with hardware and software teams to support simulation-to-reality transfer

title: Mechanical Intern
jobDescription: The chassis, drivetrains, enclosures, and mounts that hold our robots together have to take impact, vibration, and loaded operation, and keep working. As a Mechanical Intern, you will support the design, prototyping, assembly, and testing of the mechanical systems behind our UGVs. You will move between CAD, the fabrication shop, and the assembly bench, seeing parts go from a model to hardware on a robot. If you have designed your own parts, run a 3D printer, and built real mechanical assemblies, this internship is built for you. Key Responsibilities Support mechanical design and modelling in CAD (Solid Works, Fusion 360, or Creo) Prepare manufacturing drawings with appropriate dimensions and tolerances Assist in prototyping through 3D printing, machining, and fabrication Build and assemble mechanical subsystems: chassis, drivetrains, mounts, and enclosures Support design-for-manufacturing reviews and component selection Conduct mechanical testing: load, vibration, fitment, and endurance checks Maintain bills of materials and keep design documentation up to date Support the integration and field teams during robot assembly

title: PLC Intern
jobDescription: Behind every robot is a set of test rigs, ground support equipment, and manufacturing automation, and PLC-based control systems make those run. As a PLC Intern, you will support the programming, wiring, and commissioning of industrial control systems used across our test and production environments. This is a hands-on role spanning ladder logic, control panels, and the sensors and actuators that close the loop. If you have programmed a PLC, wired a control panel, and worked with industrial sensors, this internship is built for you. Key Responsibilities Assist in PLC programming using ladder logic and structured text Support control panel wiring, I/O mapping, and point-to-point testing Integrate and verify industrial sensors, actuators, and drives Help build and configure HMI screens for test rigs and automation Support the setup and commissioning of automated test stations Troubleshoot control logic and field wiring faults Document control schematics, I/O lists, and program logic Collaborate with mechanical and electronics teams on automated test setups

title: Senior PCB Design Engineer
jobDescription:
Apply for Senior PCB Design Engineer at Acceleration Robotics.

Role Overview:

We are seeking an experienced and detail-oriented Senior PCB Designer with 5+ years of professional experience to join our h RESPONSIBILITIES: Design multi-layer PCBs (4 to 12+ layers) for embedded systems, motor controllers, power electronics, and sensor interfaces. Develop schematics and layouts from concept through production-ready designs with DFM/DFA considerations. Implement high-speed design techniques for USB, Ethernet, CAN, and other communication interfaces. Ensure signal integrity, power integrity, and EMC/EMI compliance through proper design practices. Create and maintain component libraries, schematic symbols, and PCB footprints. Coordinate with fabrication and assembly vendors for prototyping and production runs. Support hardware bring-up, debugging, and design validation of PCB prototypes. Generate comprehensive documentation, including schematics, BOMs, assembly drawings, and fabrication notes. Collaborate with embedded software, mechanical, and systems teams on integrated hardware solutions. Mentor junior designers and establish PCB design guidelines and best practices. Requirements & Qualifications Bachelor's or Master's degree in Electronics Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or related field. Minimum 5 years of professional experience in PCB design and development with a production-proven track record. Proficiency in Altium Designer (strongly preferred), and Ki Ca D. Extensive experience with multi-layer PCBs (4+ layers), stack-up planning, and impedance-controlled routing. High-speed design experience with USB, Ethernet, HDMI, LVDS and associated layout constraints. Experience designing power supplies, motor drivers, and battery management systems. Proficiency in mixed-signal layout with proper analog/digital isolation techniques. Strong understanding of EMC/EMI design principles, grounding, and filtering techniques. Hands-on experience with microcontrollers (STM32, ESP32, ARM Cortex) and motor drivers (DC, BLDC, stepper). Familiarity with communication interfaces: CAN, RS485, SPI, I2C, UART, Ethernet, USB. Experience with power management circuits: DC-DC converters, LDOs, battery charging, and protection circuits. Experience with industrial, automotive, or ruggedized application designs preferred. Perks & Benefits Opportunity to work with an amazing team of like-minded engineers Learn and grow as a robotics developer. You will get to work on new and exciting applications Competitive salary Ready to Apply? Take the next step in your career. Submit your application and we'll review it promptly. title: Power Electronics Engineer
jobDescription: Moving heavy robots through rough terrain, steep inclines, and long duty cycles takes power systems that hold up under peak demand and sustained field abuse. As a Power Electronics Engineer, you will design the power backbone of our UGVs: battery systems and BMS, DC-DC converters, motor drive power stages, and the protection that keeps it all safe. You will own these designs from topology and prototype through validation and field debugging. If you have designed power stages that survive peak loads, thermal stress, and real-world abuse, this role is built for you. Day-to-Day Activities Design power electronics for UGV platforms: DC-DC converters, motor drive power stages, and inverters Design and integrate battery packs and battery management systems (BMS) Engineer for high current, thermal management, and efficiency across the duty cycle Select magnetics, passives, and power semiconductors for performance and reliability Design protection circuits for overcurrent, overvoltage, and thermal events Prototype, test, and validate power systems under load and thermal stress Ensure EMI/EMC compliance of power subsystems Coordinate with the motor drive, PCB, and mechanical teams on integration Debug power-related faults observed in the lab and in the field

title: Embedded Firmware Engineer
jobDescription:
Job description

The firmware running on our robots has to be real-time, reliable, and field-hardened, because a missed deadline or an unhan Job description The firmware running on our robots has to be real-time, reliable, and field-hardened, because a missed deadline or an unhandled fault shows up as a robot stuck in the field. As an Embedded Firmware Engineer, you will write the firmware that runs our UGV subsystems: motor controllers, sensor nodes, power management, and safety logic. You will own code from architecture through hardware bring-up, on-vehicle testing, and field debugging. If you have shipped firmware that runs on robots, vehicles, or hardware out in the field, this role is built for you. Day-to-Day Activities Develop embedded firmware in C/C++ on ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers (STM32 and similar) Implement real-time control loops for motor control, sensor sampling, and actuation Build and maintain communication stacks: CAN, UART, SPI, I2C, and Ethernet Develop RTOS-based applications and bare-metal firmware as appropriate Implement bootloaders and over-the-air / field update mechanisms Build fault handling, watchdogs, and safety logic into every subsystem Integrate sensors and actuators and support hardware bring-up with the electronics team Debug at the hardware level using oscilloscopes, logic analysers, and JTAG/SWD Write firmware tests, support validation, and maintain documentation and version control Requirements & Qualifications Requirements and Qualifications 5+ years of professional embedded firmware development experience Degree in Electronics, ECE, Computer Science, or a related field Strong C and C++ for embedded systems Deep experience with ARM Cortex-M microcontrollers, bare-metal and RTOS (e.g. Free RTOS) Hands-on experience with communication protocols: CAN essential, plus UART/SPI/I2C Experience writing peripheral drivers and real-time control code Strong hardware debugging skills with oscilloscopes, logic analysers, and debuggers Proficiency with version control (Git) and disciplined documentation Preferred Skills (Good to Have) Experience with motor control firmware, including Field-Oriented Control (FOC) Background in robotics, UGV, EV, or automotive embedded systems Exposure to functional safety practices Experience integrating firmware with ROS-based systems Python for tooling, automation, and test scripts Perks & Benefits Opportunity to work with an amazing team of like-minded engineers Learn and grow as a robotics developer. title: Robotics Software Engineer - Outdoor Autonomy
jobDescription: Our robots have to navigate unstructured outdoor terrain, rough ground, slopes, dust, and GPS-degraded environments, safely and predictably. As a Robotics Software Engineer for Outdoor Autonomy, you will own the autonomy stack that makes that possible: localisation, mapping, planning, perception, and the safety logic that surrounds them. You will take autonomy from development through field tuning on real vehicles. If you have shipped outdoor autonomy on real ground robots, and you know how navigation breaks when the GPS drops and the terrain gets ugly, this role is built for you. Day-to-Day Activities Develop and deploy the outdoor autonomy stack: localisation, mapping, path planning, and navigation, in ROS/ROS2 Implement sensor fusion across GPS/GNSS, IMU, Li DAR, cameras, and wheel odometry Build SLAM and state estimation that hold up in GPS-degraded and GPS-denied environments Develop terrain-aware path planning and obstacle avoidance for unstructured ground Build perception for outdoor, unstructured environments Implement behaviour and mission logic together with safety and fallback layers Integrate autonomy with motion control and operator interfaces Run field tests, tune the stack, and debug autonomy behaviour on real vehicles Build logging, telemetry, and replay tooling that gives the team visibility into autonomy decisions

title: Deployment Engineer - Robotics
jobDescription: A robot is only as good as its worst day in the field, and finding that worst day before the customer does is exactly what this role exists for. As a Test and Deployment Engineer, you will plan and run the testing that proves our UGVs are ready, then take them from the lab into integration, commissioning, and field deployment. You will work hands-on across mechanical, electrical, and software, and you will spend real time at field sites. If you like breaking robots to find what fails, and you are equally comfortable on a test bench and at a dusty field site, this role is built for you. Day-to-Day Activities Plan and run structured test campaigns: functional, endurance, environmental, and field testing Build test rigs, fixtures, and repeatable test procedures Integrate, commission, and validate complete robotic systems Support field deployment and customer-site operations Capture, log, and analyse test data to evaluate robot performance Identify, document, and track failures and defects through to resolution Coordinate with design teams on fixes and verify the iterations that follow Maintain test documentation, procedures, and reports Support acceptance testing, demonstrations, and operator training

title: Mechanical Design Simulation Engineer
jobDescription:
Job description

Before a part is ever cut, it has to survive in simulation: shock, vibration, fatigue, thermal load, and the sustained abus Job description Before a part is ever cut, it has to survive in simulation: shock, vibration, fatigue, thermal load, and the sustained abuse a UGV takes in the field. As a Mechanical Design Simulation Engineer, you will own the structural, dynamic, and multi-body simulation of our UGV mechanical systems: chassis, drivetrains, suspensions, mounts, and mechanisms. You will use FEA and multi-body dynamics to predict how designs behave, catch failures early, and steer design decisions with data rather than guesswork. If you have used ANSYS, MSC Adams, and similar tools to take real mechanical designs from model to validated, field-proven hardware, this role is built for you. Day-to-Day Activities Run structural, modal, fatigue, and thermal FEA on UGV mechanical components and assemblies in ANSYS Build and run multi-body dynamics (MBD) simulations of drivetrains, suspensions, and mechanisms in MSC Adams Model shock, vibration, and durability load cases representative of real field operation Correlate simulation results with physical test data and refine models accordingly Translate simulation findings into concrete design recommendations for the mechanical team Define load cases, boundary conditions, and material models together with the design and test teams Support lightweighting, stiffness, and durability optimisation of components Document simulation setups, assumptions, results, and conclusions clearly Build reusable simulation workflows, templates, and best practices Requirements & Qualifications Requirements and Qualifications 5+ years of professional mechanical simulation experience (FEA and/or multi-body dynamics) Degree in Mechanical, Aerospace, or Automotive Engineering Strong hands-on expertise with ANSYS (Mechanical, structural, and explicit dynamics) Hands-on experience with MSC Adams or an equivalent multi-body dynamics tool Solid grounding in structural mechanics, dynamics, vibration, and fatigue Experience with material models, contact, and nonlinear and dynamic analyses Proven track record of correlating simulation with physical test results Strong CAD literacy (Solid Works, Creo, or similar) and clear technical documentation Preferred Skills (Good to Have) Experience with explicit dynamics, shock, and drop simulation (LS-DYNA, ANSYS Explicit) Exposure to thermal, CFD, or coupled multiphysics analysis Experience with robotics, automotive, off-road, or heavy-vehicle mechanical systems Scripting for simulation automation (Python, APDL, or macros) Experience with optimisation and design-of-experiments methods Perks & Benefits Opportunity to work with an amazing team of like-minded engineers title: PLC Programmer - Robotics
jobDescription: Behind the robots are the test rigs, ground support equipment, and manufacturing automation that keep development and production moving, and PLC-based control systems run all of it. As a PLC Programmer, you will design, program, and commission the industrial control and automation systems behind our test and production environments. You will own control logic end to end, from I/O architecture and panel design through HMI, commissioning, and field troubleshooting. If you have programmed and commissioned PLC systems end to end, and you take pride in control logic that is safe, clean, and well documented, this role is built for you.
